blocking_defects.defect: Three closing problems. (1) n8 'UTMB says it will keep evaluating.' drops c8's object. The release says it will keep evaluating 'utilization, clinician experience' and delivery, not accuracy. (2) The citations clipped to the chart from s1, plus s8 'The question rides back to the chart edge with its sources', show the question and answer being filed into one patient's record. c1 only supports access to cited evidence from within the EHR. blocking_defects.criterion: dominant_action + source truth (human action claimed; visual certainty exceeds the source)
blocking_defects.defect: The narration claims human actions that nobody performs. 'A UTMB clinician types a question' and 'Clinicians sign in' are done by a card that fills itself on a wall (A), keys that press themselves and keep pressing in reverse while the card slides away (B), and a badge on a cord from nowhere (both). 'types' is not in c4, which says 'ask'. A physical badge-tap reader is a hardware design; c3 says only 'standard UTMB enterprise credentials', and MODERN_FILM forbids inferring hardware design.
blocking_defects.fix: In B, add anonymous scrub-sleeved hands and forearms entering from frame bottom: no face or identity, planted wrists, key-down synced to finger contact, one push that sends the card. For sign-in, the hands type a blank masked credential and a lock on the 'Health record' boundary opens in the same shot. Drop the badge reader. Narration n1a: 'A UTMB clinician asks a question.' If credible limbs can't be built in this medium, rewrite n1a and n3a so no clinician action is the pictured subject. Never keep a ghost performer.

blocking_defects.defect: The narration never says 'AI' or 'OpenEvidence', and the tool that docks in s2 is an unlabelled teal tab. A viewer can't tell that an AI tool is answering; it could be search or a librarian. That is the actor of the whole story.
blocking_defects.fix: Name the tool within c1, e.g. n2a 'UTMB announced the OpenEvidence AI tool on September twenty-second,' or name it in n1b. Label the docked tab 'OpenEvidence' and make it visible from s1 as the place the question goes and the answer comes from. s2 then only lights the boundary and attaches the date tags. This also heads off the likely false inference that the patient chart, or patient data, produces or receives the answer.

consolidated_correction: One correction on B that keeps the 8-scene spine, the claims and the scene roles. No voice take has been spent (tts_calls 0), so the script edits are cheap now. Narration: n1a 'A UTMB clinician asks a question.'; n2a names the OpenEvidence AI tool within c1; n8 'UTMB says it will keep evaluating use and clinician experience.' Picture: (1) A labelled OpenEvidence tool is docked at the 'Health record' boundary from s1 and is where the question goes and the answer comes from. (2) One question card and one answer card with one citation set, which never clips to the patient chart. (3) Masked slot insert and extract, with no pops, and the extended send event fills the gap before the answer returns. (4) Anonymous hands perform sign-in (masked credential, boundary lock opens in frame) and typing; the badge reader and cord are removed. (5) Every tag pinned, sized to its text, glyph clear of type. (6) Limit tags read 'Not in release' and attach to the answer card, whose Sources slot fills while its Accuracy slot stays visibly empty. That one object carries s6 and s7. (7) Overlays on a clean surface. (8) Cuts after decisive events, and the jump cuts replaced. (9) Labels needed for comprehension sit in medium or closer shots at 30 px or more, inside x 36-918 and above the caption band. (10) The close holds the answer with its sources and empty slots beside the chart, with the corrected evaluation tag on the usage share. (11) Re-bind story_art action_uses to B's views and set interior:true.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: Intended chain at code scope, not observed: a question goes out of one patient chart and an answer comes back with three source-type cards. Date tags mark the September 22nd announcement and March go-live. A sign-in unlocks the chart and a plain-language question is typed. The citation cards name literature and guidelines. More than half of a tile wall lights for decision support. The share is tagged as UTMB's own report, and accuracy and patient-care tags hang open. A thread links the answer to its citation while a 'Right?' ring stays empty. The close says UTMB will keep evaluating. As coded, a viewer is never told this is AI or OpenEvidence. A's opening shows the question, not the answer, coming back. Both closes suggest UTMB is evaluating accuracy.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The opening asks what comes back when a clinician asks inside the record. The ending should answer: an answer with its sources, and nothing in the release showing whether it is right. Currently the ending re-performs the question's return and attaches an evaluation tag whose object (use and clinician experience) is missing, which turns an honest limit into an implied accuracy review.
story_review.weakest_transition: s7 to s8: the unmarked answer cuts to the question re-performing its return into the chart and an evaluation tag hung beside the accuracy and patient-care tags. This repeats the setup, implies answers are filed into the patient record and implies UTMB is evaluating accuracy.
